title.en: Why does lab-grown muscle bend this joint so little, and every build differently?
title.ja: 培養筋肉で動くこの関節は、なぜ少ししか曲がらず、一つ一つ違うのか？ (check)

steps.stimulate: {{n_builds_page}} builds of the same joint, because no two muscle rings are alike.
steps.fixed_force: Published design tools for these robots give every muscle the same fixed force. [C13] [C24]
steps.rings_heavy: Heavy load: the swing grows from {{swing_heavy_n1:.0f}}° to {{swing_heavy_n4:.0f}}° with more rings.
steps.rings_light: Light load: {{swing_light_n1:.0f}}° to {{swing_light_n4:.0f}}°. Rings buy torque, not travel.
steps.spread: Where does the spread sit? This is what my experiment will test.
steps.rebuild_rings: Same rings, rebuilt: little changes. Fix that fits: add a spare ring.
steps.rebuild_assembly: Same rings, rebuilt: your joint changes. Fix that fits: rebuild the stack.
steps.rebuild_combination: Same rings, rebuilt: nothing changes. Fix that fits: swap rings or grow a new batch.
steps.shield: My model: ×{{shield_ratio:.2f}}. Measured: about ×2. One of my assumptions is probably wrong. [C4]

readouts.no_balance: builds without a balance point (joint at its stop)

sobol_caption: Shares depend on the illustrative ranges I chose.

explain.rings: Muscle rings are loops of lab-grown muscle. A stack of them sits on each side of the hinge.
explain.stimulate: Stimulate one side: its rings contract and turn the joint, while the stretched rings on the other side pull back.
explain.spread: No two rings are alike, so every build of the same joint swings differently. Stray field also reaches the other side.

tips.badge: Every angle and force on this page comes from a simplified model, not from lab measurements.
tips.parity: Green when the page's model reproduces the reference numbers in oracle.json exactly.
tips.clip: The lab's antagonistic actuator, stimulated left and right (Movie S11). The simulated joint follows the clip's timing until you take over.
tips.stimulate: Stimulate one stack electrically; press again to release. The sides take turns.
tips.fixed: Make every ring identical, as most simulators assume. The spread between builds disappears.
tips.rings: How many muscle rings each stack holds. More rings give more force, not much more swing.
tips.spread: Choose which source of differences between builds dominates: the rings, the assembly of a stack, or which rings end up together.
tips.rebuild: Take your joint apart and assemble it again from the same rings.
tips.shield: Walls that keep the stimulating field away from the other stack, so it is not stimulated by mistake.
tips.load: How hard the hinge resists turning: a light or a heavy load.
tips.new: Draw a new set of builds.
tips.typical: The median build: half the builds swing more, half less.
tips.worst: One build in ten swings less than this.
tips.chance: The share of builds that reach the target swing.
tips.rest: Your joint's angle before stimulation: uneven stacks make it lean.
tips.blocked: How hard your joint's stimulated stack pulls if the joint is held straight.
tips.you: Your joint: one of the builds. B rebuilds it from the same rings.
tips.median: The typical build: the median angle.
tips.builds: Every other build of the same design, one line and tip each.
tips.band: The lab's actuator turned this much on average, from short to long stimulation (Fig. 6E of the paper). [C19]
tips.target: The swing a design should reach.
tips.ring_on: A stimulated stack: its rings contract.
tips.ring_off: A relaxed stack: stretched by the joint, its rings pull back.
tips.bars: The share of the spread between builds each source causes. Bar: in total, together with the others. Tick: on its own.
tips.g_rings: Each ring pulls with its own strength.
tips.g_assembly: How a stack is put together: the whole stack pulls a little more or less. Changes when you rebuild.
tips.g_combination: Which rings end up in the same stack. Stays the same when you rebuild.
tips.g_crosstalk: How much of the stimulating field reaches the other stack.
tips.ring: A muscle ring: a loop of lab-grown muscle hooked over two posts. It pulls when stimulated and when stretched.
tips.base: The fixed side of the joint: one end of every ring hooks onto a post here.
